Jonas — quick technical write-up and list of deliverables below. TL;DR: we can satisfy AcmeX with two supported paths; one is config change on Dedicated/Private, the other is an export-based guarantee for Hosted.

Options (technical):
A) Dedicated/Private: per-tenant retention configuration (90d)
   - Implementation: retention TTL is a configurable parameter in the tenant profile stored in the control plane. For Dedicated/Private we can expose an override and push a policy to serving nodes.
   - Evidence: control-plane change log (immutable audit entry), config dump (JSON) showing TTL=90, screenshot of UI tenant settings.
   - Constraints: requires Dedicated or Private deployment. For Hosted customers we don't expose persistent per-tenant TTL changes today for multi-tenant runtime.

B) Hosted — Export & Attestation (workable for most customers)
   - Implementation: scheduled log snapshot job (daily or weekly) that exports tenant logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket with server-side encryption and object lifecycle set to >=90d; objects are versioned and signed.
   - Evidence: export job run history (timestamped logs), sample exported object list (filenames + checksums), runbook for reconstitution, attestation PDF.
   - Constraints: requires customer S3 bucket + acceptance of exported-format (we deliver JSONL with schema). Cost: extra egress + storage; recommend weekly exports to limit egress cost while meeting 90d window.

Artifacts we can produce (deliverable pack):
- redwood-retention-matrix.csv (matrix describing default vs options)
- runbook-log-export.md (step-by-step for S3 export, includes IAM policy snippet)
- config-dump-tenant-XXXX.json (sanitized sample)
- export-job-history.log (redacted run entries)
- attestation_acmex_90d.pdf (1 page letter on retention enforcement)

I'll attach the matrix and runbook drafts. If they require the full CAIQ control ID crosswalk, we can map each artifact to control IDs (quick task).

Neha Kapoor
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Lauren / Tom — thanks for the note and for attaching the SIG spreadsheet. Below is a concise proposal to satisfy the 90-day forensic requirement; please pick which option you prefer and we will produce the supporting artifacts within the listed SLAs.

Option 1 — Dedicated / Private tenant TTL override (recommended if you require server-side enforcement)
  - What we deliver: per-tenant TTL configured to 90 days, control-plane audit log extract, sanitized config dump, UI screenshot showing TTL, and a signed attestation.
  - Timeline: 7-10 business days after contract amendment / provisioning.
  - Requirements: Dedicated or Private deployment; pricing amendment (storage + support).

Option 2 — Hosted export + attestation (recommended if you want faster delivery)
  - What we deliver: weekly export to customer S3 (JSONL), export job history (logs), sample object checksums, runbook, and a signed attestation.
  - Timeline: 3-5 business days to enable export + initial evidence pack once S3 is provisioned.
  - Requirements: customer-owned S3 bucket and an acceptance of exported artifacts. There will be a modest monthly managed export fee.

Artifacts to expect in either path: redwood-retention-matrix.csv, runbook-log-export.md, export-job-history.log, attestation_acmex_90d.pdf, and a one-page mapping of artifacts to SIG/CAIQ control IDs.

Next steps:
1) Confirm preferred option (1 or 2) and whether you can provide an S3 bucket for exports.
2) If Option 1, we will loop in sales/legal for an amendment and provide estimated commercial terms.
3) If Option 2, please share S3 bucket ARN and an IAM role we can assume (I will share the IAM snippet).

I'll attach a draft mutual action plan and the quick artifact list; happy to jump on a call to walk through.

Best,
